items.whyNow: On 28 Sep Yemen's army claimed 356 operations and 476 Houthis killed or wounded in 24 hours across ten fronts and bombed Houthi positions at Al-Rubaie west of Taiz, the WHO put the toll at 164 dead and 645 injured for 19–26 Sep (4,481 casualties and 838 deaths since 6 Aug, more than 180,000 displaced), EU foreign policy chief Kallas said the bloc will seek observer status in the Saudi-led maritime coalition and expand the six-ship Aspides mission to escort through Bab al-Mandab, Saudi Arabia resumed crude exports through the repaired East-West pipeline, Riyadh's schools stayed online to 1 Oct, and three Iranian-made drones hit a PDKI camp near Erbil at dawn two days before the coalition's exit from Iraq. Singapore-bound routings still depend on a Houthi-held Bab al-Mandab, and the Houthis have not fired at Saudi cities since 26 Sep.
changes: 28 Sep: Yemen armed forces spokesman Col. Majid al-Nuzaili said 356 operations over 24 hours across ten fronts from Haradh and al-Tuwal in Hajjah to the west coast, Saada, al-Jawf, Marib, Lahj, Taiz and al-Bayda killed or wounded 476 Houthis and destroyed command centres and depots, accusing the Houthis of turning schools into command posts, and the Taiz Military Axis said its aircraft bombed Houthi positions at Al-Rubaie west of Taiz plus sites in Lahij and Al-Dhalea, with no Houthi comment (party claims, unverified); Sanaa's military media released footage of a Turkish-made Karayel drone it said was downed over Al-Tinah in Hajjah, a claim first made on 27 Sep and not independently verified (Anadolu, Anews, Yemen Press Agency, InvestingLive).

28 Sep: The WHO recorded 809 casualties (164 deaths, 645 injuries) in Yemen between 19 and 26 Sep, bringing the total since 6 Aug to 4,481 including 838 deaths, with Lahj the heaviest front and more than 180,000 displaced; Kaja Kallas said the EU will apply for observer status in the new Saudi-led maritime defence coalition and asked ministers to expand the six-ship Aspides mission to escort cargo through Bab al-Mandab ('the need is bigger than it's ever been'); Saudi Arabia resumed oil exports through the East-West pipeline repaired after the 10 Sep drone strikes; AFP traced a viral 'Riyadh airport' fire video to a June drone attack on a Moscow shopping centre (Anadolu/MEMO, AP via KSAT, Al Arabiya, CBS News live, AFP via Yahoo).

28 Sep: Three Iranian-made drones struck the PDKI's Azadi camp at Koy Sanjaq southeast of Erbil at dawn, causing material damage but no deaths, the third attack on the camp this year; the Iraqi armed forces spokesman told Rudaw the Erbil withdrawal is under way and no foreign troops will remain after 30 Sep, and the cabinet declared a four-day 'Sovereignty Days' holiday from 30 Sep (Anadolu, Rudaw via Hatha Alyoum, Shafaq News).

27 Sep: Riyadh's schools moved to remote learning on the Madrasati platform, now confirmed to run from 27 Sep to 1 Oct with no ministry explanation, a day after the coalition intercepted two Houthi drones headed for the capital and two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait; no Houthi launch at Saudi Arabia has been reported since (The National, AsiaNews, The Media Line).

27 Sep: Two air strikes hit a market at Taiz's Mawiya junction: Al-Masirah said seven were killed and 40 wounded, Saree put casualties near 50 and blamed Saudi F-15s, warning of 'severe consequences', Houthi sources told AFP about 30 fighters and eight civilians died, and Yemen's government said its forces hit a Houthi camp and vehicles near the market; Critical Threats logged strikes on the Istiqlab camp in Mawiyah, a Houthi official Nour al-Din al-Marani reportedly killed near al-Hawban and Southern Giants drone strikes on Jabal Kahboub, while the army claimed 756 operations, 2,316 Houthis hit and four Iranian experts killed over 72 hours (AFP via CP24, Critical Threats, Arab News, Al Jazeera).

26 Sep: Coalition spokesman al-Maliki announced the interception of two Houthi drones headed for Riyadh and two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait; Saree claimed 27 Saudi strikes on bridges and roads including the al-Dalil bridge on the Sanaa–Taiz route and Houthi officials threatened Saudi command-and-control sites over 'red lines'; the GCC called the attacks a 'grave escalation' and SCMP reported that Pakistan and Turkey have limited their Makkah-pact response to statements after the 25 Sep chiefs-of-staff meeting (Arab News, Critical Threats, SCMP, Asharq Al-Awsat).

next.text: Arrival and first engagement of the French radar and air-defence detachment at Yanbu (no numbers or dates given since Macron's 24 Sep announcement), whether Rafales, UK, Italian, Greek or Gulf assets join, whether EU ministers approve Kallas's 28 Sep request to expand Aspides and grant the EU observer status in the Saudi-led coalition, and whether the Houthis attack the deployments themselves.
next.ifSeen: A hit on French-protected infrastructure or French casualties → escalate on outside-force stakes; Aspides expansion approved → note for the monthly pattern set on escort; no arrival by mid-October → treat the pledge as declaratory.

next.text: Makkah pact follow-through after the 25 Sep Riyadh chiefs-of-staff meeting, which SCMP on 26 Sep found had produced only statements: Pakistani or Turkish air-defence batteries, interceptors, aircraft, intelligence cells or ammunition actually arriving in Saudi Arabia, or a joint command being named.
next.ifSeen: Batteries or a joint command deployed → note for the monthly pattern set on coalition point defence; nothing beyond communiqués → pact remains political.

next.text: End of the lull since 26 Sep and Houthi follow-through on Saree's 27 Sep 'severe consequences' warning over the Taiz market strike: a launch that leaks through and hits Khamis Mushait, Taif, Yanbu or Riyadh, a return to the two-day rhythm (19, 24, 26 Sep) or a salvo rate above one a day for a week, a strike on a Saudi command site, or a hit on the reopened East-West pipeline or Yanbu loadings.
next.ifSeen: Leak-through with damage or casualties, or a pipeline or Yanbu hit → escalate the same day; sustained daily salvos → note interceptor consumption for the monthly pattern set; lull past 3 Oct with schools reopened → note de-escalation.

next.text: Effect of al-Alimi's general mobilisation and the amnesty opened 26 Sep, and whether the claimed 356-a-day operational tempo and the Jabal Bazel and Jabal Nouman gains are held: reported enlistment, tribal levies on the Al-Sabiha and Taiz fronts, or notable Houthi defections (none reported by 28 Sep); WHO weekly casualty reports as the independent check on tempo.
next.ifSeen: Verified defections or new brigades at the front → note for the monthly pattern set; no visible effect → treat as declaratory.

next.text: Government forces lose the Kahboub heights or the Taiz–Aden road (Hayjat al-Abd pass), giving the Houthis the overlook of Bab al-Mandab from both shores, or Bab al-Mandab daily crossings fall below 20 for a week (last count 27 on 24 Sep), or a Houthi hit on a non-Saudi hull before the Gemini SE1 Suez transit due 27 Oct.
next.ifSeen: Any of these → flag today; Singapore-bound routings shift to the Cape; SE1 transit completed unmolested → note for the monthly pattern set on route recovery.

next.ifSeen: Drone strikes on Erbil city or Harir after coalition air defence leaves → escalation indicator; KH/Nujaba refusal of the plan → note for the monthly pattern set.

ignore.note: The 356 operations and 476 casualties on 28 Sep, like the 756 and 2,316 figures on 27 Sep, are Yemeni army claims with no independent check; the WHO's 164 deaths and 645 injuries for 19–26 Sep are the only independent tally and cover all parties. The Karayel drone footage is Houthi military media only; the CGTN and InvestingLive items relay the same 27 Sep Saree claim, and an earlier Karayel shoot-down over Hajjah was claimed on 10 Sep, so do not count it as a new type. The Taiz market strike remains contested (seven killed and 40 wounded per Al-Masirah, about 30 fighters and eight civilians per Houthi sources to AFP, a Houthi camp per Yemen's government), with no Saudi comment found. The Riyadh school closure has no official reason. The Erbil drone attack is attributed only by drone origin ('Iranian-made', unnamed party source). The EU observer status has no defined operational meaning yet. The Al-Monitor shipping piece is paywalled; the SE1 transit dates come from its preview. No Bab al-Mandab crossing count was found for 25–28 Sep and nothing new was found on Israel–Syria; absence of reporting is not confirmation.

timeline.text: The Houthis declare a naval and air blockade of Saudi Arabia in response to a strike on Sanaa airport, ending four years of relative calm under the 2022 truce.
Drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province hit Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline in Riyadh and Medina provinces; Riyadh shuts the line the next day and Brent tops $100.
Houthi forces seize Perim Island and the last stretch of Yemen's Red Sea coast a day after taking Mocha, gaining control of Bab al-Mandab and reiterating a ban on Saudi ships.
The Houthis fire a ballistic missile and drones at Riyadh for the first time in this escalation; Saudi Arabia says it was intercepted as smoke rises near King Khalid airport.

Ahead of the 30 September coalition exit from Iraq, the prime minister moves militia disarmament to a phased plan ending in June 2027 behind a 90-day halt in attacks, as Syrian President Sharaa says security talks with Israel reached about 90 percent before Israel pulled back.

After the Houthis fire a mixed missile and drone barrage at Jazan, Yanbu, Taif and Riyadh and Saudi Arabia intercepts six ballistic missiles, President Macron announces French soldiers, radars and air-defence systems for the Yanbu terminal and the Makkah pact foreign ministers agree in New York to convene their chiefs of staff.

The coalition intercepts two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait and two drones headed for Riyadh, Riyadh's schools move online for a week, and a strike on a market at Taiz's Mawiya junction the next day kills at least seven by Houthi count as Yemen's army claims 756 operations in 72 hours.

The WHO counts 164 dead and 645 injured in Yemen in a week as the army claims 356 operations in a day, the EU seeks observer status in the Saudi-led maritime coalition, Saudi crude exports resume through the East-West pipeline, and Iranian-made drones hit a PDKI camp near Erbil two days before the coalition leaves Iraq.

text: On long-range attack versus layered protection, the Rising · Contested status is borne out: the Houthi salvos of 19, 24 and 26 Sep were all intercepted by the coalition's account and none has followed through 28 Sep, yet Riyadh's schools stay online to 1 Oct, so the effect is disruption bought by threat, not damage. Protection thickens on paper faster than in the field: the Yanbu detachment has no dates, SCMP found on 26 Sep that Pakistan and Turkey had offered statements not batteries, and Kallas's 28 Sep bid for EU observer status adds a naval layer of undefined meaning, while East-West pipeline exports resumed on 28 Sep. On maritime disruption versus route resilience, the Established · Contested status holds: Bab al-Mandab stays Houthi-held, the army's claimed 356 operations on 28 Sep (single source) and the 27 Sep drone strikes on Jabal Kahboub contest the overlook, and Gemini carriers are scheduling a Suez transit for 27 Oct, betting that the Houthi ban stays Saudi-specific.

On regional basing versus militia targeting, the Established · Contested status is confirmed by the 28 Sep drone hit on the PDKI camp near Erbil, the third this year, two days before the coalition's exit: deniable strikes on Iranian opposition targets will be the first test of Baghdad's promise to keep weapons in state hands once coalition air defence leaves; Israel–Syria stays frozen since 23 Sep.
